en brødkniv.explanation: "En brødkniv" means "a bread knife", the long knife with small teeth that cuts bread without crushing it: Brug brødkniven til det friske brød (Use the bread knife for the fresh bread).

sentence.da: Han skærer det friske brød med en **brødkniv**.
sentence.en: He cuts the fresh bread with a bread knife.

en brødkurv.explanation: "En brødkurv" means "a bread basket". It is built from brød (bread) and kurv (basket): Brødet ligger i brødkurven (The bread is in the bread basket).

sentence.da: Tjeneren stiller en **brødkurv** på bordet.
sentence.en: The waiter puts a bread basket on the table.

en brødrister.explanation: "En brødrister" means "a toaster". It is built from brød (bread) and at riste (to toast): Jeg lægger to skiver i brødristeren (I put two slices in the toaster).

sentence.da: Jeg putter to skiver brød i min **brødrister**.
sentence.en: I put two slices of bread in my toaster.

en brøk.explanation: "En brøk" means "a fraction", a part of a whole in math: Én halv (½) er en brøk (One half is a fraction).

sentence.da: Læreren viser os en **brøk** på tavlen.
sentence.en: The teacher shows us a fraction on the board.

en buffet.explanation: "En buffet" means "a buffet". Jeg tager mad fra buffeten means "I take food from the buffet".

sentence.da: Vi tager selv mad fra den store **buffet**.
sentence.en: We take food ourselves from the big buffet.

en bund.explanation: "En bund" means "a bottom", the lowest part of something: Der er kaffe i bunden af koppen (There is coffee at the bottom of the cup). It is also the base of a pie: en tærtebund (a pie crust).

sentence.da: Kassen har en tynd **bund**.
sentence.en: The box has a thin bottom.

en bunke.explanation: "En bunke" means "a pile", things lying on top of each other in a loose heap: en bunke tøj (a pile of clothes). It also means "a lot": en bunke penge (a lot of money). Compare with en stak (a stack), which is neat.

sentence.da: Der ligger en stor **bunke** tøj på gulvet.
sentence.en: There is a big pile of clothes on the floor.

en burger.explanation: "En burger" means "a burger", a patty of meat in a bun. A vegetarian one is en vegetarburger (a vegetarian burger).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **burger**.
sentence.en: I would like a burger.

en bus.explanation: "En bus" means "a bus". To say you go by bus, use at tage bussen (to take the bus) or at køre med bus (to travel by bus).

sentence.da: Vi kører med **bus** til skolen.
sentence.en: We travel by bus to school.

en busbillet.explanation: "En busbillet" means "a bus ticket", built from bus (bus) and billet (ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **busbillet** til bussen.
sentence.en: I buy a bus ticket for the bus.

en buschauffør.explanation: "En buschauffør" means "a bus driver". The word chauffør (driver) works for other vehicles too: en taxachauffør (a taxi driver), en lastbilchauffør (a truck driver).

sentence.da: Jeg spørger en **buschauffør** om vej.
sentence.en: I ask a bus driver for directions.

en busk.explanation: "En busk" means "a bush", a plant with many stems close to the ground: Der er en busk ved huset (There is a bush by the house). Fuglen gemmer sig i busken (The bird hides in the bush).

sentence.da: Der sidder en lille fugl i en **busk**.
sentence.en: A small bird is sitting in a bush.

en butik.explanation: "En butik" means "a shop", usually a smaller one that sells one kind of thing, such as clothes or shoes. For a big shop with food and everyday things, Danes say et supermarked (a supermarket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber sko i en **butik** i byen.
sentence.en: I buy shoes in a shop in town.

en butiksindehaver.explanation: "En butiksindehaver" means "a shop owner", the person who owns and runs a shop: Butiksindehaveren står selv i kassen (The shop owner stands at the register personally).

sentence.da: Han er **butiksindehaver** og åbner selv butikken hver morgen.
sentence.en: He is a shop owner and opens the shop himself every morning.

en by.explanation: "En by" means "a town" or "a city". Danish uses one word for both, so it can be small or big. I byen means "in town", and Jeg skal ind til byen means "I am going into town".

sentence.da: Der er mange huse i en **by**.
sentence.en: There are many houses in a town.

en bydel.explanation: "En bydel" means "a district", one part of a city: Nørrebro er en bydel i København (Nørrebro is a district in Copenhagen). It is built from by (town) and del (part).

sentence.da: Vi bor i en rolig **bydel** nær havnen.
sentence.en: We live in a quiet part of town near the harbor.

en byge.explanation: "En byge" means "a shower", a short burst of rain: Der kommer en byge om lidt (A shower is coming soon). For washing yourself, use et brusebad (a shower).

sentence.da: Der kom en kraftig **byge**, og vi blev våde.
sentence.en: A heavy shower came and we got wet.

en byggeplads.explanation: "En byggeplads" means "a construction site". It is built from bygge (build) and plads (place): Man skal have hjelm på byggepladsen (You must wear a helmet at the construction site).

sentence.da: Han arbejder på en **byggeplads** i byen.
sentence.en: He works on a construction site in the city.

en båd.explanation: "En båd" means "a boat", from a small rowboat to a bigger one. For a big ship, Danish uses et skib (a ship).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **båd** til øen.
sentence.en: We are taking a boat to the island.

en bæltetaske.explanation: "En bæltetaske" means "a fanny pack", a small bag worn around the waist: Jeg har pas og penge i min bæltetaske (I have my passport and money in my fanny pack).

sentence.da: Hun har sine nøgler i en **bæltetaske**.
sentence.en: She has her keys in a fanny pack.

en bænk.explanation: "En bænk" means "a bench", a long seat for several people, often in a park: Der er en bænk ved søen (There is a bench by the lake).

sentence.da: Vi sætter os på en **bænk** og hviler.
sentence.en: We sit down on a bench and rest.

en bærbar computer.explanation: "En bærbar computer" means "a laptop". Bærbar (portable) means you can carry it: Jeg tager min bærbare computer med på arbejde (I take my laptop with me to work).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **bærbar computer** i min taske.
sentence.en: I have a laptop in my bag.

en bøde.explanation: "En bøde" means "a fine", money you must pay as a punishment: Jeg fik en bøde for at cykle uden lys (I got a fine for biking without a light). Use at få en bøde (to get a fine).

sentence.da: Jeg fik en **bøde**, fordi jeg parkerede forkert.
sentence.en: I got a fine because I parked in the wrong place.

en bøf.explanation: "En bøf" means "a steak", a piece of cooked meat, most often beef. A ground-meat patty is en hakkebøf (a ground beef patty).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have en **bøf** med kartofler.
sentence.en: I would like a steak with potatoes.

en bøjle.explanation: "En bøjle" means "a hanger", for hanging clothes in a closet: Hæng jakken på en bøjle (Hang the jacket on a hanger). The same word is in en tandbøjle (braces for teeth).

sentence.da: Jeg hænger skjorten på en **bøjle**.
sentence.en: I hang the shirt on a hanger.

en bølge.explanation: "En bølge" means "a wave" in the water: Børnene hopper i bølgerne (The children jump in the waves). It is also used for other waves: en hedebølge (a heat wave).

sentence.da: En stor **bølge** ramte båden.
sentence.en: A big wave hit the boat.

en børnehave.explanation: "En børnehave" means "a kindergarten", for children from about three to six, before school starts. It is built from børn (children) and have (garden).

sentence.da: Min datter er fire og går i **børnehave**.
sentence.en: My daughter is four and goes to kindergarten.

en børnemenu.explanation: "En børnemenu" means "a kids' menu", a smaller meal for children at a restaurant. It is built from børn (children) and menu (menu).

sentence.da: Har I en **børnemenu** til mit barn?
sentence.en: Do you have a kids' menu for my child?

en børste.explanation: "En børste" means "a brush", for hair, shoes or cleaning: Jeg bruger en børste til gulvet (I use a brush for the floor). The same word is the verb at børste (to brush): Jeg børster tænder (I brush my teeth).

sentence.da: Jeg har en blød **børste** til mit hår.
sentence.en: I have a soft brush for my hair.

et bad.explanation: "Et bad" means "a bath" or "a shower". To take one, say at tage et bad (to have a bath or shower). Do not mix it up with et badeværelse (a bathroom) or at bade (to swim or bathe).

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **bad** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I take a shower every morning.

et badekar.explanation: "Et badekar" means "a bathtub", a tub you fill with water and lie in: Hun ligger i badekarret (She lies in the bathtub). A bruser (shower) has no tub.

sentence.da: Hun lægger sig i et **badekar** og slapper af.
sentence.en: She lies down in a bathtub and relaxes.

et badeværelse.explanation: "Et badeværelse" means "a bathroom", the room with the shower or bath. It is made from bad (bath) and værelse (room). To find a public toilet, ask for et toilet (a toilet), not badeværelse.

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **badeværelse** med bad.
sentence.en: We have a small bathroom with a shower.

et bagagebånd.explanation: "Et bagagebånd" means "a baggage carousel", the moving belt where you pick up your bags at the airport: Tasken kommer på bagagebåndet (The bag comes on the baggage carousel). It is built from bagage (baggage) and bånd (belt).

sentence.da: Vi venter ved **bagagebånd** nummer to.
sentence.en: We are waiting at baggage carousel number two.

et bagagerum.explanation: "Et bagagerum" means "a trunk", the storage space at the back of a car. It is built from bagage (luggage) and rum (room): Kufferten ligger i bagagerummet (The suitcase is in the trunk).

sentence.da: Vores nye bil har et stort **bagagerum**.
sentence.en: Our new car has a big trunk.

et bageri.explanation: "Et bageri" means "a bakery". To buy something there, you can say Jeg vil gerne have et rundstykke (I would like a bread roll).

sentence.da: Jeg køber brød og kager i et **bageri**.
sentence.en: I buy bread and cakes in a bakery.

et band.explanation: "Et band" means "a band", a group that plays music: Vi har et band (We have a band). Do not mix it up with et bånd (a ribbon or tape).

sentence.da: Vores **band** spiller til en fest i morgen.
sentence.en: Our band is playing at a party tomorrow.

et barn.explanation: "Et barn" means "a child", and also your own child at any age: mit barn (my child). The plural børn looks quite different from barn: to børn (two children).

sentence.da: Hun har et lille **barn** hjemme.
sentence.en: She has a small child at home.

et barnebarn.explanation: "Et barnebarn" means "a grandchild", literally a child's child, built from barn (child): Min mormor har fem børnebørn (My grandmother has five grandchildren).

sentence.da: Min mormor elsker sit nye **barnebarn**.
sentence.en: My grandmother loves her new grandchild.

et batteri.explanation: "Et batteri" means "a battery", in a phone, a car or a toy: Bilen har et nyt batteri (The car has a new battery). A battery is fladt (dead) when it has no power left.

sentence.da: Mit **batteri** er næsten tomt.
sentence.en: My battery is almost empty.

et bed.explanation: "Et bed" means "a flower bed", a patch of soil in a garden: Der er røde tulipaner i bedet (There are red tulips in the flower bed). For a bed to sleep in, use en seng (a bed).

sentence.da: Der er mange røde blomster i mit **bed**.
sentence.en: There are many red flowers in my flower bed.

et behov.explanation: "Et behov" means "a need", something you must have: Børn har et behov for søvn (Children have a need for sleep). With for, it says what is needed.

sentence.da: Der er et stort **behov** for lærere.
sentence.en: There is a great need for teachers.

et beløb.explanation: "Et beløb" means "an amount" of money, for example on a bill: Hvad er beløbet? (What is the amount?) For an amount of other things, use en mængde (a quantity).

sentence.da: Det samlede **beløb** er tusind kroner.
sentence.en: The total amount is a thousand kroner.

et ben.explanation: "Et ben" means "a leg" and also "a bone"; the situation tells you which. Han har brækket benet literally says the leg, but means "He has broken his leg". The plural is the same as the single word: to ben (two legs).

sentence.da: Han har brækket sit **ben**.
sentence.en: He has broken his leg.

et besøg.explanation: "Et besøg" means "a visit". The plural is the same as the single word: to besøg (two visits). To be visiting someone, say på besøg: Jeg er på besøg hos min mor (I am visiting my mother).

sentence.da: Tak for dit **besøg**! Kom snart igen.
sentence.en: Thank you for your visit! Come again soon.

et betalingskort.explanation: "Et betalingskort" means "a payment card", a debit or credit card you pay with. It is made from betaling (payment) and kort (card). The plural is the same as the single word: to betalingskort (two cards).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler med mit **betalingskort**.
sentence.en: I pay with my payment card.

et bevis.explanation: "Et bevis" means "a proof", and also "evidence": Det er et klart bevis (That is clear proof). Politiet har ikke noget bevis (The police have no evidence).

sentence.da: Jeg tror dig ikke uden et **bevis**.
sentence.en: I do not believe you without proof.

et bibliotek.explanation: "Et bibliotek" means "a library". You say at låne en bog på biblioteket (to borrow a book at the library).

sentence.da: I et **bibliotek** kan man låne bøger gratis.
sentence.en: In a library you can borrow books for free.

et bibliotekskort.explanation: "Et bibliotekskort" means "a library card", the card you show to borrow books: Har du dit bibliotekskort med? (Do you have your library card with you?). It is built from bibliotek (library) and kort (card).

sentence.da: Jeg viser mit **bibliotekskort** og låner tre bøger.
sentence.en: I show my library card and borrow three books.

et billede.explanation: "Et billede" means "a picture", such as a photo, a painting or an image on a screen. Say at tage et billede (to take a picture) and at hænge et billede op (to hang up a picture). Et foto (a photo) is more specific.

sentence.da: Jeg tager et **billede** af dig.
sentence.en: I am taking a picture of you.

et bjerg.explanation: "Et bjerg" means "a mountain". A smaller, lower one is en bakke (a hill). It is also part of longer words, like en bjergtur (a mountain trip).

sentence.da: Vi går op på et stort **bjerg**.
sentence.en: We walk up a big mountain.

et blad.explanation: "Et blad" means "a magazine" and also "a leaf": Hun læser et blad (She is reading a magazine). Træet har grønne blade (The tree has green leaves).

sentence.da: Jeg læser et **blad** på toget.
sentence.en: I read a magazine on the train.

et blik.explanation: "Et blik" means "a look", a quick glance or the expression in someone's eyes: Han kastede et blik på uret (He glanced at the clock). Hun har et venligt blik (She has a kind look).

sentence.da: Hun så på mig med et trist **blik**.
sentence.en: She looked at me with a sad look.

et blinklys.explanation: "Et blinklys" means "a turn signal", the light that tells others you are about to turn: Jeg bruger blinklyset (I use the turn signal). It is blink (blink) plus lys (light).

sentence.da: Husk at bruge **blinklys**, når du drejer.
sentence.en: Remember to use your turn signal when you turn.

et blåbær.explanation: "Et blåbær" means "a blueberry". It is built from blå (blue) and bær (berry). Blåbær gør tungen blå (Blueberries turn your tongue blue).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser **blåbær** med mælk om morgenen.
sentence.en: I eat blueberries with milk in the morning.

et boardingpas.explanation: "Et boardingpas" means "a boarding pass", the paper or phone ticket you show to get on a plane. Do not mix it up with et pas (a passport).

sentence.da: Jeg viser mit **boardingpas** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: I show my boarding pass at the airport.

et bogstav.explanation: "Et bogstav" means "a letter" of the alphabet: A er det første bogstav (A is the first letter). A letter you mail is et brev (a letter).

sentence.da: Hvilket **bogstav** kommer efter B?
sentence.en: Which letter comes after B?

et bord.explanation: "Et bord" means "a table". In a restaurant, you can ask Et bord til to, tak (A table for two, please). A desk is et skrivebord (literally a writing table).

sentence.da: Bogen ligger på et **bord**.
sentence.en: The book is lying on a table.

et brev.explanation: "Et brev" means "a letter" that you send in the post. For an email, say en mail (an email). At skrive et brev means "to write a letter".

sentence.da: Jeg skriver et **brev** til min mor.
sentence.en: I write a letter to my mother.

et brugernavn.explanation: "Et brugernavn" means "a username", the name you use to log in to a website or app: Hvad er dit brugernavn? (What is your username?) It is built from bruger (user) and navn (name).

sentence.da: Skriv dit **brugernavn** i feltet her.
sentence.en: Write your username in the field here.

et brusebad.explanation: "Et brusebad" means "a shower", the kind you take to wash. The verb is at tage (to take): Jeg tager et brusebad efter træning (I take a shower after exercise).

sentence.da: Jeg tager altid et **brusebad** om morgenen.
sentence.en: I always take a shower in the morning.

et bruseforhæng.explanation: "Et bruseforhæng" means "a shower curtain". It is built from bruse (to shower) and forhæng (curtain): Bruseforhænget holder vandet inde i badet (The shower curtain keeps the water inside the shower).

sentence.da: Vi skal købe et nyt **bruseforhæng** til badeværelset.
sentence.en: We need to buy a new shower curtain for the bathroom.

et bryllup.explanation: "Et bryllup" means "a wedding". You can say you are going to one with til bryllup: Vi skal til bryllup (We are going to a wedding). At holde bryllup means "to hold a wedding".

sentence.da: Vi skal til **bryllup** i dag.
sentence.en: We are going to a wedding today.

et bryst.explanation: "Et bryst" means "a chest", the front of the upper body, and it can also mean "a breast". Danish often says the chest instead of my chest: Jeg har smerter i brystet means "I have pain in my chest".

sentence.da: Hjertet slår i mit **bryst**.
sentence.en: The heart beats in my chest.

et bræt.explanation: "Et bræt" means "a board", a flat piece of wood: Der ligger et bræt på gulvet (There is a board on the floor). It is also part of brætspil (board game) and skærebræt (cutting board).

sentence.da: Jeg saver et **bræt** over med en sav.
sentence.en: I saw a board in two with a saw.

et brætspil.explanation: "Et brætspil" means "a board game", a game played on a board: Vi har mange brætspil derhjemme (We have many board games at home). It is built from bræt (board) and spil (game).

sentence.da: Vi spiller et **brætspil** om aftenen.
sentence.en: We play a board game in the evening.

et budget.explanation: "Et budget" means "a budget", a plan for what money comes in and goes out: Vi laver et budget hver måned (We make a budget every month). To stay within it, say at overholde budgettet (stick to the budget).

sentence.da: Vi har et lille **budget** til ferien.
sentence.en: We have a small budget for the vacation.

et busstoppested.explanation: "Et busstoppested" means "a bus stop". It is made from bus (bus) and stoppested (a place where something stops). People often shorten it to et stoppested (a stop).

sentence.da: Jeg venter på bussen ved et **busstoppested**.
sentence.en: I am waiting for the bus at a bus stop.

et bål.explanation: "Et bål" means "a bonfire" or "a campfire", an open fire outdoors: Vi tænder et bål på stranden (We light a fire on the beach). A fire that destroys things is en brand: Der er brand i huset (The house is on fire).

sentence.da: Vi sidder rundt om et **bål** og griller pølser.
sentence.en: We sit around a bonfire and grill sausages.

et bælte.explanation: "Et bælte" means "a belt". Et sikkerhedsbælte (a seat belt) is built on the same word, from sikkerhed (safety).

sentence.da: Jeg har et sort **bælte** på.
sentence.en: I am wearing a black belt.

et bær.explanation: "Et bær" means "a berry". Many berry names end in bær: jordbær (strawberry) and blåbær (blueberry).

sentence.da: Jeg plukker et **bær** fra busken og spiser det.
sentence.en: I pick a berry from the bush and eat it.

et børneværelse.explanation: "Et børneværelse" means "a children's room", the room in a home where the kids sleep and play. It is built from børn (children) and værelse (room): Børneværelset er lyst (The children's room is bright).

sentence.da: Der er mange bamser i vores **børneværelse**.
sentence.en: There are many teddy bears in our children's room.
